title: Format an arithmetic table
description: Write a function `arithmetic_table(a, b)` that returns a multi-line string showing `a + b`, `a - b`, `a * b`, `a / b` (rounded to 2 decimals), `a % b`, `a // b`, and `a ** b`, one operation per line in the form `a OP b = result`.
hints: Idea to consider: one f-string line per operator, joined with \n
Each line follows the same shape - f'{a} OP {b} = {result}' - so building a list of these lines and joining them with '\n' avoids repeating the same string-building logic seven times.
Compute all seven results, format each into its own line with the matching operator symbol, and join the lines with \n.
expected_behavior: Returns the seven operations formatted one per line, in the order shown.
solution:
def arithmetic_table(a, b):
    lines = [
        f"{a} + {b} = {a + b}",
        f"{a} - {b} = {a - b}",
        f"{a} * {b} = {a * b}",
        f"{a} / {b} = {round(a / b, 2)}",
        f"{a} % {b} = {a % b}",
        f"{a} // {b} = {a // b}",
        f"{a} ** {b} = {a ** b}",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)
explanation: Building a list of already-formatted lines and joining them once at the end mirrors the join_words pattern from earlier in this same day - the same technique for combining multiple pieces of text into one.
